policy: Mutation-critical file list (#330). The PR gate mutates changed lines in exactly these files plus the nightly sweep measures them first. The list only grows monotonically: removing or weakening an entry requires a governance-approved change recorded in the reason/evidence fields. Tests that inspect source text or compare constants to their own defaults are not evidence for these properties (see #320, #321, #322); only killed mutants count.

entries.reason: The constant-time secret comparison primitive. #320 demonstrated the compare_digest -> == mutant survives source-inspection tests; the live decision must route through compare_digest.

Resource-security floors (rate limit, body caps, circuit breaker, active-run ceilings). #321 demonstrated the 100x rate-limit and 1024x body-limit mutants survive tests that compare production constants to themselves; the oracle is quality/security-resource-floors.json.

Privilege checks including the live admin-key bypass. #322 demonstrated a secret_equal -> == mutation on the active comparison is the real bypass; every authorization decision must be exercised through the public boundary.
Router scorer magnitudes decide which model/agent serves a request; an off-by-one or sign flip silently changes routing class without failing any functional test.
Memory decay magnitudes decide what the agent forgets. A weakened decay threshold retains stale or poisoned context with no functional failure.
Memory consolidation decides what is promoted to durable memory; a mutated guard can promote unvetted content.
PII sensitivity tiers gate which observability payloads may leave the workspace; weakening a band check leaks PII on normal-tier events (ADR-055 / SPEC-070226-2b70).
Persona rubric thresholds decide pass/fail scoring boundaries; a nudged comparison operator or magnitude changes acceptance verdicts invisibly.
